link_description: SINGAPORE - A decade after being introduced, Project Wolbachia – an initiative to control dengue through the release of lab-grown mosquitoes – now covers over half of all households in Singapore. Following a launch in Ang Mo Kio on Oct 6, Project Wolbachia now covers more than 840,000 households – or 53% of all households here – covering most of the areas at risk of large dengue outbreaks. This was announced on Oct 31 by Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment Janil Puthucheary at an event marking the initiative’s 10th anniversary, held at Our Tampines Hub. Beginning in 2016, Project Wolbachia aims to control the Aedes mosquito population here via the release of male mosquitoes infected with the Wolbachia bacteria. Female mosquitoes that mate with these males produce eggs that do not hatch, thus reducing the mosquito population over time. In February, research published in the New England Journal of Medicine found that the Aedes aegypti mosquito populations were reduced by 80 to 90% in areas covered by Project Wolbachia, while the dengue risk for residents in these areas fell by over 70%.
